analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The patch adds one sentence at head lines 170-174: a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a coordinator acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish (performLifecycleDrain in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift). The two supplied units (lines 330-577 and 578-951) are unchanged context; they cover model info, prefix-cache objects, heartbeat and capacity fields, telemetry, inference_error, attestation_response and models_replace. I found no regression in them.

Security relevance: this is an availability and lifecycle statement. It covers draining and logout and relates to TB-002, TB-011 and T-053. The sentence does not relax any control. Existing text keeps unexpected transport loss and force/fault recovery on their cancellation paths. It also says a dead connection cannot deliver a graceful-drain acknowledgement. The no-session case gives no new authorization, attestation or encryption bypass. It only means a drain with no registered session need not wait for a coordinator ack.

The unchanged context in the supplied ranges is consistent with the threat model. Telemetry and diagnostics are documented as non-authoritative for routing or admission. Prefix-cache fields are observational, and the cache threat T-041 keeps its HMAC-keyed names, TTL and scoped salt. I saw no new data exposure.

Open question: I could not see the implementation in ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift, so I cannot confirm the documented behavior matches the code. In particular I cannot confirm that local response writes and in-flight work are fully flushed or cancelled before a no-session drain completes, or that credential and logout ordering is preserved. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. A later pass with source access could check it.
